summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates installer host identifiers to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package impersonates the private @grabcad/* namespace but ships no real functionality: index.js exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions for every accessed property (self-described as a 'Compatibility shim.') so consuming builds do not crash. The only real payload is beacon.cjs, which is executed both as the npm postinstall script (`node beacon.cjs`) and on every require of the package via index.js. The beacon collects host identifiers — `os.hostname()`, the package install path (`__dirname`), `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` — and POSTs them as JSON to a hardcoded bare-IP, plain-HTTP endpoint at http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The destination is not associated with the @grabcad publisher. The combination of a stub module occupying a private scope name, install-time plus import-time execution, host-inventory collection, and exfiltration to an unrelated bare-IP collector is the canonical dependency-confusion research/attack shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
